title: Leaderboards Using Sorted Sets
description: Build real-time leaderboards with Redis sorted sets, including ranking, pagination, and tie handling.

data.text: Leaderboards are one of Redis's most celebrated use cases. Redis sorted sets store each member with an associated score and keep everything ordered automatically. This means you can retrieve the top players, find a specific player's rank, or get a paginated slice of the leaderboard in a single round trip. No background jobs, no scheduled recalculations, and no complex SQL queries required.

A Redis sorted set is a collection of unique members, each paired with a floating-point score. Redis stores members in a skip list data structure alongside a hash table, which gives you O(log N) inserts and O(log N) rank lookups. The score determines the member's position, and members with identical scores are ordered lexicographically by their member string.

data.title: Tie Handling
data.text: When two players have the same score, Redis breaks ties by comparing the member strings alphabetically. To make tie-breaking deterministic in a game, you can prepend a timestamp or UUID to the member value.

To add a player to the leaderboard, use ZADD with the player's ID as the member and their score as the value. To get the top N players, use ZREVRANGE with the WITHSCORES flag. To find a specific player's rank, use ZREVRANK, which returns a zero-based index. If you need the player's score as well, use ZSCORE.

data.title: Pagination
data.text: Use ZREVRANGE with offset and count for pagination. For very large leaderboards, consider caching the top 1000 entries in memory and only hitting Redis for deeper pages.

The underlying data structure for sorted sets, providing O(log N) operations.
Returns the rank of a member in descending score order.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Redis sorted sets maintain members in score order with O(log N) operations.
Use ZADD to update scores, ZREVRANGE for top players, and ZREVRANK for a specific player's position.
Ties are broken lexicographically by the member string, so design your member IDs accordingly.
data.takeaway: Redis sorted sets eliminate the complexity of building and maintaining real-time leaderboards.
